description: Mayfair outpost of Manish Mehrotra's New Delhi fine-dining Indian — modernist technique on Old India dishes.
tips: Paired tasting menus are exceptional.

name: Bibi
description: Chet Sharma's JKS-Group Mayfair restaurant — reinterpreting Indian subcontinent cooking through a fine-dining lens.
tips: Michelin-starred. Book 3-4 weeks ahead.

name: Soutine
description: Corbin & King's all-day brasserie in St John's Wood — the most Parisian-feeling restaurant north of the Thames.
address: 60 St John's Wood High St, London NW8 7SH
tips: Brunch here is a weekend tradition.

name: BRAT x Climpson's Arch
description: A summer-residency outdoor grill by BRAT's Tomos Parry — a 30-seater at Climpson's Arch railway arch in London Fields.
tips: Summer only. Book months ahead.

name: Mao Chow
description: Sichuan in Hackney — dan-dan noodles and spicy wontons, a tiny Kingsland Road favourite.
tips: Walk-in. Cash-preferred.

name: Xi'an Impression
description: A tiny Holloway Road café beside Arsenal's Emirates — hand-pulled biang-biang noodles, cumin lamb, pork and chilli burgers.
tips: Biang-biang noodles and pork burger essential.

name: Dumplings' Legend
description: Chinatown's Shanghai-style xiaolongbao specialist — soup dumplings made in the front window; a Gerrard Street classic.
tips: Soup dumplings the must-order. Walk-in crowd.

name: Banh Mi Bay
description: Fresh Vietnamese banh mi on Theobald's Road — proper crusty baguettes, pâté, pickled carrot, chilli.
tips: BBQ pork banh mi a classic. Takeaway-friendly.

name: Song Que
description: Kingsland Road Vietnamese institution since 2001 — pho, bun bo hue, and the best banh xeo pancakes in Shoreditch.
tips: BYOB allowed. Part of the Kingsland Road 'Pho Mile' strip.

name: Mien Tay
description: Vietnamese Pho Mile restaurant specialising in southern and Mekong Delta cuisine — grilled seafood and claypot dishes.
tips: Grilled monk fish in turmeric is a speciality.

name: Kappacasein Dairy
description: A Bermondsey arch cheesemaker famed for its £9 raclette toastie and grilled cheese — one of London's true single-dish destinations.
tips: Open Saturdays only at Maltby Street Market. Expect a queue.

name: Monty's Deli
description: Fleet Street-reviving Jewish deli in Hoxton — pastrami sandwiches, matzo ball soup, pickled herring, cheesecake.
tips: Pastrami and rye is essential. Open into evenings.

name: Som Saa's Spitalfields Original
description: The Blue Posts upstairs restaurant in Soho — the Palomar team's 60-seater, with a theatre-kitchen view.
tips: Genuinely good value in the West End — book ahead.

name: Sabrage — English Sparkling Bar
description: West End champagne bar specialising in English sparkling wine — a free educational tasting comparison with Champagne.
tips: English sparkling flights £28. Food pairings available.

name: Swift Cocktails Soho
description: Two-floor drinking den on Old Compton Street — upstairs pre-dinner, downstairs speakeasy whiskey bar.
tips: Irish coffee a signature. 150+ whiskies downstairs.

name: Morgan M
description: Morgan Meunier's long-standing Clerkenwell French restaurant — classical, quiet, Michelin-star fine dining.
tips: Tasting menu pairs with French Burgundy.

name: Mere
description: Monica Galetti's Fitzrovia restaurant — contemporary European in a calm basement, the MasterChef professional's home kitchen.
tips: Three-course lunch £38.

name: Yauatcha City
description: The Square Mile branch of the all-day dim sum favourite — in a sleek Broadgate Circle space.
tips: Try the macarons downstairs — petit fours for the bar.

name: Lyaness
description: Mr Lyan's Sea Containers bar — world-class cocktails built on 'ingredients we make ourselves'.
tips: Tasting flights available. Food menu is snacks-only.

name: Blue Elephant
description: Royal Thai in Fulham's Imperial Wharf — opulent gilded setting, classic Thai menu, big on fruit carvings.
address: The Boulevard, Imperial Wharf, London SW6 2UB
tips: Sunday brunch champagne menu a weekend classic.

name: Aquavit London
description: St James's Scandi-fine-dining restaurant — herring, pickled beetroot, venison, and an interior of pale woods and bright lamps.
address: St James's Market, 1 Carlton St, London SW1Y 4QQ
tips: Set lunch £29. Open daily.

name: Ekstedt at The Yard
description: Swedish fire-and-smoke cooking at the Great Scotland Yard Hotel — food cooked over birch, juniper and open coals, no electricity.
tips: Tasting menu only. Dinner from 6pm.

name: Hide Above
description: The Michelin-starred upper floor of Hide in Mayfair — modern British tasting menu with Green Park views.
tips: Ground-floor Hide & Seek is cheaper with same kitchen.

name: Borough Market Small-Plates Tour
description: A self-guided food tour of Borough Market stalls — the Bread Ahead doughnut, Kappacasein toastie, Ottolenghi, Brindisa tapas.
tips: Saturday is peak. Weekdays quieter. Go hungry.

name: Akoko
description: Fitzrovia West African restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand, tasting menu spans Sierra Leone, Nigeria, Ghana.
tips: Tasting menu only. Book weeks ahead.

name: Chishuru
description: Adejoke Bakare's Fitzrovia West African restaurant — a seasonal menu celebrating a pan-African pantry, Michelin-starred 2024.
tips: Tasting menu £65. First female African chef to win a Michelin star in the UK.

name: Yayah's — Golden Chippy
description: A legendary fish-and-chip-shop on Greenwich's Blackheath Road with a tuk-tuk on the roof — proper British chippy, Caribbean-accented.
tips: The cod fillet is massive. Jerk chicken dishes a cult pick.

name: Goddards at Greenwich
description: An East End-style pie-and-mash shop that has moved to Greenwich — proper jellied eels, meat pie, liquor, since 1890.
tips: Pie, mash, liquor, jellied eels all £8 each. Cash preferred.

name: M. Manze Pie and Mash
description: The oldest surviving pie-and-mash shop (1902) — Tower Bridge Road institution, tile-walled, Grade II-listed interior.
tips: Closes at 4pm. Cash only. Order pie + mash with liquor — the green parsley sauce is the secret.

name: Café OTO
description: Experimental-music café and venue in Dalston — gigs many nights, a daytime café, and a brilliantly curated record/book shop.
tips: Gig-only access in the evenings. Great record shop upstairs.

name: Tramshed
description: A Mark Hix restaurant in Shoreditch (now closed but iconic)
tips: Under redevelopment 2026 — check before visiting.

name: Popolo
description: Shoreditch pasta and small plates bar — Italian seasonal cooking, walk-in and counter-style, endlessly buzzy.
tips: Walk-ins at counter only; tables bookable.

name: Saint Leonards
description: A smart Shoreditch restaurant cooking over open fire and raw-bar seafood — a statement of modern-British ambition.
tips: Whole grilled fish is the signature move.

name: Rotorino
description: Stevie Parle's Dalston southern-Italian restaurant — handmade pasta, wood-oven pizza, and a lively bar.
tips: Sunday lunch excellent — bring friends.

name: Jolene
description: Jeremy Lee-style Newington Green restaurant and bakery — big windows, open kitchen, Parisian café feel.
tips: Bakery takeaway from 8am. Small daily menu.

name: Westerns Laundry
description: A sister to Primeur — industrial-chic Highbury corner restaurant serving immaculate seafood and natural wine.
tips: Whole fish special is always excellent.

name: Primeur
description: Canonbury corner restaurant serving small plates to share — natural wine, French-inflected cooking, lively atmosphere.
tips: Walk-in-friendly at counter. Book for tables.

name: Planque
description: Kingsland Road restaurant and wine club — industrial setting, immaculate small-plates, serious wine cellar.
tips: Cellar membership gives access to rare-vintage offers.

name: Forza Wine
description: A Peckham rooftop wine bar and restaurant — natural wines and Italian small plates, sunset views.
tips: Arrive early for sunset — Thursday is packed.

name: Levan
description: A Peckham natural-wine restaurant — sister to Forza Wine with more substantial plates and a big open kitchen.
tips: Open late. Try the natural fizz.

name: Peg
description: Jonathan Lawson's Hackney yakitori and natural-wine bar — hot counter seats overlooking the grill.
tips: Sister restaurant Legs a block away.

name: Legs
description: Hackney's Broadway Market restaurant — small plates, Italian-leaning, a big wine list.
tips: Pasta changes daily. The pici is always excellent.

name: Lahpet
description: Burmese restaurant in Shoreditch — tea-leaf salad, fish-curry mohinga, a lively bar scene.
tips: Tea-leaf salad is the house signature.

name: Zia Lucia
description: Islington pizzeria with a 48-hour dough and an ink-black charcoal crust — a new-wave London pizza classic.
tips: Charcoal dough is the signature. 10 branches now.

name: Pizza Pilgrims Dean St
description: Soho's beloved Neapolitan pizzeria — brothers James and Thom Elliott opened their first bricks-and-mortar here in 2013.
tips: Lots of branches. Margherita classic; Nutella pizza ring the closer.

name: Franco Manca Brixton
description: The original Franco Manca in Brixton Market — sourdough Neapolitan pizza for under £10, now a household name.
tips: Walk-in only. Lunch queues move fast.

name: Ace Pizza London Fields
description: Tom Kerridge's pizzeria on the edge of London Fields — sourdough Neapolitan, a strong natural wine list.
tips: Book or walk-in. 'Ace' pizza is a must try.

name: Burger & Lobster Mayfair
description: Single-concept cult restaurant — choose a burger, lobster, or lobster roll for £26. Five locations; Mayfair is the original.
tips: Walk-in. Lobster roll is the pick.

name: Patty & Bun Soho
description: Smashed burger specialist on James Street — the Ari Gold burger with smoky mayo has a cult following.
tips: Queue or walk-in. 10+ branches across London.

name: Shake Shack Covent Garden
description: The original UK Shake Shack in Covent Garden's Piazza — reliable smashburgers, crinkle fries, and concretes.
tips: Al fresco seating in the Piazza is lovely.

name: Bleecker Burger
description: New York-style smashburger joint with multiple central branches — short menu, thin patties, no frills, pure craft.
tips: Cheeseburger and black and blue burger are the picks.

name: Supawan
description: Thai family restaurant in King's Cross — neighbourhood classic with genuine regional dishes like khao soi and boat noodles.
tips: Northern-Thai menu; khao soi is the must-order.

name: Berenjak
description: Soho's candle-lit Persian grill house — Kay Khatami's charcoal skewers, fluffy rice, and bright mezzes.
tips: Taftoon bread is baked in the centre of the dining room.

name: Persia Restaurant
description: Long-running Peckham Iranian restaurant — ghormeh sabzi, kabab koobideh, and hearty rice dishes, all under £20.
tips: BYOB. Family-run.

name: Morito Hackney Road
description: The Hackney Road branch of Moro's tapas sister — Eastern Mediterranean small plates, big dining room.
tips: Walk-in at counter; book tables.

name: Fenchurch at Sky Garden
description: 35th-floor fine dining beneath the dome at Sky Garden — a Michelin-adjacent seafood-forward menu with panoramic views.
tips: Book ahead. Entry via Sky Garden lift.

name: Darwin Brasserie at Sky Garden
description: Sky Garden's casual 36th-floor brasserie — pre/post-theatre menus, best skyline-dining value in the City.
tips: Book 3-course lunch £35.

name: Sky Pod Bar
description: Sky Garden's 35th-floor bar — cocktails with a 360° view, and free garden admission if you're drinking.
tips: Book a table in advance for sunset.

name: Koffmann's at The Berkeley
description: Pierre Koffmann's fine-dining in the basement of the Berkeley Hotel — classical French, Michelin-starred precision.
tips: Lunch £40 — bargain for Michelin food.

name: Bar Boulud
description: Daniel Boulud's Knightsbridge brasserie under the Mandarin Oriental — French-American, excellent burgers, a fine wine list.
tips: The BB burger is a signature.

name: Park Chinois
description: Mayfair's 1930s-Shanghai-themed Chinese restaurant — live cabaret, opulent interiors, a dinner-theatre vibe.
tips: Book Club Chinois downstairs for live cabaret.

name: The Dining Room at Claridge's
description: Simon Rogan's fine-dining inside the iconic Art Deco hotel — British ingredients, three Michelin stars at its peak.
tips: Jacket required. Arrive early for a cocktail in the Foyer.

name: The Foyer & Reading Room, Claridge's
description: One of the world's most famous afternoon teas — under mother-of-pearl chandeliers, with Art Deco opulence.
tips: Book 2 months ahead. Dress smart.

name: The Goring Dining Room
description: The UK's only family-owned grand hotel's restaurant — a Royal Warrant holder, where Kate Middleton ate her pre-wedding dinner.
tips: Sunday lunch trolley roast is a national treasure.

name: Berners Tavern
description: Jason Atherton's all-day restaurant inside the London EDITION hotel — astonishing high-ceilinged room lined with hundreds of paintings.
tips: Brunch set £35 weekends.

name: Angler
description: Moorgate fine-dining seafood restaurant on top of South Place Hotel — a roof terrace, Michelin-starred cooking.
tips: Set lunch £45. Rooftop bar open summer.

name: City Social
description: Jason Atherton's 24th-floor City restaurant — Art Deco, Michelin-starred, and all Canary Wharf-to-St-Paul's skyline.
address: Tower 42, 25 Old Broad St, London EC2N 1HQ
tips: Bar on the same level is walk-in-friendly.

name: Ember Yard
description: Salt Yard Group's Basque-inspired tapas bar in Berwick Street — wood-fire grilling, and a small-plates menu.
tips: Sister to Salt Yard, Dehesa, and Opera Tavern.

name: Salt Yard
description: The original Anglo-Spanish-Italian tapas bar in Fitzrovia — pioneered the small-plate movement in London.
tips: Fritto-misto and courgette flowers are the signatures.

name: Opera Tavern
description: Covent Garden's Iberian-Italian tapas bar — gorgeous Victorian pub downstairs, intimate counter upstairs.
tips: The mini Iberico-pork burger is essential.

name: Dehesa
description: Carnaby Street tapas stalwart — ham-and-cheese counter, cross-Spanish menu, great sherry list.
tips: Sit at the counter for the full jamón experience.

name: Barrafina Adelaide Street
description: Sam & Eddie Hart's original Catalan tapas counter — standing-only, walk-in, reliably excellent.
tips: Best at opening 12pm or 5pm to secure a counter spot.

name: Barrafina Coal Drops Yard
description: The third Barrafina counter, in King's Cross — the larger space has all the same magic.
tips: Standing-room counter only. Arrive early.

name: Andina
description: Peruvian restaurant in Shoreditch — ceviche, quinoa bowls, cocktails from the land of Pisco.
tips: Ceviches are the don't-miss category.

name: Sushi Show
description: Sneaky new-wave omakase sushi counter in Marylebone — 12-course menus at £75-150.
tips: Lunch omakase £75.

name: Lita
description: Marylebone's new Mediterranean wine bar — Italian-leaning cooking, a cellar of natural wines, a sunset terrace.
tips: Wine list focus is Italy and France.

name: Norma
description: Mayfair's stylish Sicilian restaurant — a three-floor takeover with pasta on display, seafood counter, and a rooftop bar.
tips: Rooftop booked separately; lovely for aperitivi.

name: Anglo-Thai
description: Modern Thai bistro on Chiltern Street — small plates, British-grown ingredients with Thai technique.
tips: Tasting menu is the easiest way to explore.

name: Akara
description: Adejoke Bakare's Brixton second — a West African snack bar named after the Nigerian bean-fritter.
tips: All-day dining. Check current opening.

name: Behind
description: Andy Beynon's tiny Hackney seafood tasting counter (8 seats, one sitting) — a Michelin-starred omakase-of-fish.
tips: Book 3 months ahead. Four-hour experience.

name: The Tamil Prince
description: A cracking Indian gastropub in Islington — big Tamil-inflected plates, south-Indian classics, London's favourite Sunday roast 2024.
tips: Walk-in only. Sunday Indian-accented roast is a classic.

name: The Tamil Crown
description: Sister to The Tamil Prince — Islington's new big-room Tamil gastropub, with an open kitchen and small-plates menu.
tips: Book ahead. Same team, bigger room.

name: Manteca Hand Roll
description: A sister takeaway-counter concept from the Manteca team serving fresh pasta for takeaway and dine-in
tips: Check the Manteca instagram for current location and hours.

name: Morchella
description: A new mushroom-themed restaurant from the St. JOHN alumni team — St John's nose-to-tail meets forager-season mycology.
tips: Mushroom-only tasting menu.

name: The Dove
description: A Victoria Park pub with an Anglo-Belgian beer list and a walled beer garden — Hackney's favourite pre-park spot.
tips: Beer list is Belgium-heavy. Sunday roast popular.

name: Gold
description: Notting Hill's shareable Greek-Cypriot grill — the Bechara brothers' second venue after Casa Cruz.
tips: Famous for grilled meat platters for sharing.

name: The Ned Vault
description: Soul-food American dining in the former Midland Bank vault — warehouse-sized dining, plus many other restaurants upstairs.
tips: The Vault bar requires booking — 3,800 original safety deposit boxes remain.

name: Cecconi's Shoreditch
description: Soho House's Italian café at Shoreditch House — marble tables, cicchetti, long breakfasts.
tips: Bolognese with veal and pork is classic.

name: Cecconi's at The Ned
description: The big Ned Cecconi's in the grand banking hall — Venetian Italian in a banking-hall basilica.
tips: Sunday brunch jazz popular.

name: Mountain
description: Tomos Parry's new open-fire restaurant in Soho — bigger and smarter sister to Brat, Basque-influenced grilling.
tips: Whole turbot over coals is the marquee dish.

name: Chilli Cool
description: Sichuan restaurant in Bloomsbury — a genuine Chinese-student-approved spot, with proper mapo tofu and dan-dan noodles.
tips: Order off the Chinese menu. Cash preferred.

name: Oisoi
description: Pan-Asian noodles and sushi at St Katharine Docks — a long-running local favourite.
tips: Reliable neighbourhood option after Tower Bridge.

name: Kym's by Andrew Wong
description: Andrew Wong's Chinese roast-meat restaurant at Bloomberg Arcade — duck, pork belly, soy-poached chicken.
tips: Three-bird roast for 4-6 people — book ahead.

name: Kaia
description: Australasian-inspired cooking at Battersea Power Station — flame-grilled small plates, bright airy room.
tips: Good pre-cinema option at the Battersea Power Station multiplex.

name: Humble Chicken
description: Angelo Sato's yakitori counter in Soho — crispy-skin grilled skewers, an accolade-winning new-wave Japanese counter.
tips: Counter omakase £65 — fine value for the skill involved.

name: Omar's Place
description: Pimlico Mediterranean by Omar Shah — pared-back, counter-forward, warm-spirited.
tips: Seasonal menu changes often.

name: José Pizarro at Broadgate
description: Jose Pizarro's biggest venue — two floors, full tapas menu, in a light-filled Broadgate Circle location.
tips: Weekday lunch menu £22.

name: Jamavar
description: Mayfair outpost of Mumbai-fine-dining Jamavar — Michelin-starred Indian in a colonial-clubhouse setting.
tips: Lunch tasting menu £55.

name: Benares
description: Atul Kochhar's Mayfair modern Indian — Michelin-starred, with a refined dining room and creative tasting menus.
tips: Lunch thali £42 — great intro.

name: Veeraswamy
description: Britain's oldest Indian restaurant (1926) — Regent Street institution with Michelin star and gorgeous floor-to-ceiling murals.
address: Mezzanine Floor, Victory House, 99 Regent St, London W1B 4RS
tips: Pre-theatre set menu excellent.

name: Chutney Mary
description: A grand Indian in St James's — opulent dining rooms, regional Indian menu, and one of London's oldest elite Indian kitchens.
tips: Sunday buffet £49 is a hit.

name: The Cinnamon Club
description: Former Westminster library now a jewel of upscale Indian dining — Vivek Singh's empire's flagship.
tips: Pre-theatre £30. Set lunch £25.

name: Tamarind
description: Britain's first Indian restaurant to win a Michelin star (2001) — Mayfair basement with a strongly British-Indian fine-dining lens.
tips: Lunch set £29.

name: Sagar
description: A mini-chain of South Indian dosa houses — paper-thin dosas, vada, rice-and-sambar combos at honest prices.
tips: Vegetarian. The masala dosa is the must-try.

name: Nizuni
description: Charlotte Street Japanese — affordable sushi, teriyaki, and a quietly devoted Fitzrovia following.
tips: Lunch bento boxes £10-14.

name: Yoshino
description: Piccadilly Arcade basement Japanese — refined kaiseki and sushi, calm Tokyo-style atmosphere.
tips: Lunch bento £35. Weekend tasting menus only.

name: Tsuru Sushi
description: A mini-chain of reliable sushi counters — a good option for a quick bento lunch in the City.
tips: Closed evenings at some branches. Lunch-focused.

name: Atari-Ya
description: Ace sushi deli with three London branches — West End, West Hampstead, Swiss Cottage, with high-grade fish at under-£20 sushi boxes.
tips: Sushi platter takeaway is an office-worker secret.

name: Sushi Tetsu
description: Six-seat Clerkenwell omakase counter — world-famous for a reason, book months ahead.
tips: Three-month waitlist. One of London's hardest tables.

name: Koya Bar
description: The Frith Street udon counter from the Koya family — walk-in-friendly, perfect breakfast of miso porridge and udon.
tips: Opens 8:30am for breakfast — a favourite of chefs.

name: Tokii
description: Prince of Wales Hotel Japanese restaurant — the only rotating sushi kaiten in the West End with a serious kitchen behind it.
tips: Kaiten counter is fast and fun; bookable tables too.

name: Heddon Street Kitchen
description: Gordon Ramsay's all-day brasserie on Heddon Street — reliable, large-scale, and good for indecisive group dinners.
tips: Weekend brunch a popular option.

name: Petersham Nurseries Café
description: A garden-set restaurant in Richmond where greenhouse becomes dining room — Italian-leaning, seasonal, romantic.
tips: Petersham Nurseries Covent Garden is a smaller sister in town.

name: Petersham Covent Garden
description: The Covent Garden outpost of the Richmond garden favourite — La Goccia bar, Petersham restaurant, and flower shop.
tips: La Goccia cicchetti bar is walk-in friendly.

name: Emilia
description: Mercato Metropolitano pasta specialist — sfoglia rolled in the open kitchen, carbonara with pork cheek.
tips: Inside the buzzing Mercato food-hall.

name: Radio Alice
description: Hoxton Neapolitan pizza specialist — sourdough pizza, Italian wines, and open kitchen.
tips: Good local spot for a casual dinner.

name: Homeslice
description: Wood-fired 20-inch pizzas in Neal's Yard and Shoreditch — order by the slice or the whole pie.
tips: Slices from £4 — perfect quick-bite.

name: La Fromagerie
description: Cheese-and-wine merchant with dining rooms in Marylebone and Highbury — excellent cheese boards and simple lunches.
tips: Try the all-cheese board and a glass of natural wine.

name: Angelina
description: Dalston's Italian-Japanese fusion restaurant — counter seating only, short tasting menu of precise small plates.
tips: Counter only. Book weeks ahead.

name: Casa Cruz Notting Hill
description: Glamorous Argentine dining in Notting Hill — bar on one level, dining above, Argentine beef the signature.
tips: A place to be seen. Book weeks ahead.

name: Straker's
description: Tomos Parry-trained chef Tom Straker's Notting Hill restaurant — open-fire cooking, serious wine list, neighbourhood hit.
tips: Book well ahead. Try the whole turbot.

name: Planque Members Cellar
description: The members' cellar of Planque restaurant — a wine-focused private dining experience in Hackney.
tips: Membership required for cellar access.

name: Magpie
description: Pimlico's Cavendish Square small-plates hit — open kitchen, seasonal cooking, accessible pricing.
tips: Brunch weekends popular.

name: Bistrotheque
description: A Bethnal Green destination since 2004 — French bistro cooking, warehouse-style dining, a trailblazing bar.
tips: Prix-fixe lunch £25.

name: Shackfuyu
description: Japanese-American fusion in Soho — kinako French toast, kimchi cheese toastie, and a cheffy cocktail menu.
tips: Kinako French toast is an Instagram classic.

name: Flesh & Buns
description: Bone Daddies-group izakaya — Chinese-style steamed bun pockets with fillings to build yourself, loud and fun.
tips: Bottomless brunch a weekend favourite.

name: Bala Baya
description: Shay Ozer's Southwark Israeli — Tel Aviv-style platters, mezze counter, and a great-value lunch menu.
address: Arch 25, Old Union Yard Arches, 229 Union St, London SE1 0LR
tips: Bottomless lunch £38 — endless mezze.

name: Honey & Co
description: Itamar Srulovich & Sarit Packer's Middle Eastern restaurant — home cooking from Israel, Lebanon, Palestine with a crackling cake shop.
tips: Honey & Smoke next door for grill-focused menu.

name: Honey & Smoke
description: The grill-focused sister to Honey & Co — grilled meats over charcoal, hearty Israeli hospitality.
tips: Dinner Fri/Sat has the buzziest room.

name: Honey & Spice
description: The Honey & Co cake shop and deli — for home-style Middle-Eastern pastries and vivid salads to take away.
tips: Cookbook-worthy pastries.

name: Beigel Bake
description: 24-hour Brick Lane legend — salt beef bagels at 4am, £4 each, the true London late-night feed.
tips: Cash-only. Salt beef and mustard is the classic.

name: Dunn's Bakery
description: Crouch End's Victorian-era bakery since 1820 — sourdoughs, specialist breads, and the longest-running shop on Crouch End Broadway.
tips: The millionaire shortbread is legendary.

name: Beigel Shop
description: Brick Lane's yellow-shopfront bagel shop — rivals next-door Beigel Bake, devoted cult following.
tips: The hot salt beef bagel with pickle is iconic.

name: Ariana II
description: West Hampstead Afghan restaurant — mantu dumplings, qabeli palaw, and lamb kebab with basmati.
tips: BYOB. Family-run.

name: Afghan Kitchen
description: A 20-seat Islington Afghan restaurant — small menu of perfectly rendered classics, cash-preferred.
tips: Tiny — book ahead. Cash-only.

name: Mahdi
description: Hammersmith Persian restaurant — charcoal-grilled chelo kabab, smoky rice, pomegranate cocktails.
tips: Charcoal-grilled chicken is the pick.

name: Patogh
description: Marylebone's secret Persian gem — a tiny no-frills 20-seat family restaurant with the city's best chelo kabab.
tips: BYOB. Cash-only. Tiny — book ahead.

name: Ognisko
description: Kensington Polish restaurant inside the Ognisko Polskie Polish cultural centre — beautiful Victorian room, elevated Polish food.
tips: Pre-theatre £25. Duck, beetroot, pierogi.

name: Zaza Bazaar
description: A cheery Nordic-Middle Eastern neighbourhood restaurant on Brixton Hill — big tables, natural wines, communal atmosphere.
tips: Neighbourhood-first, relaxed.

name: Mama Lan
description: Brixton Village dumpling and noodle shop — hand-rolled dumplings, beef brisket noodles, a Brixton Village classic.
tips: Walk-in. Six branches now across London.

name: Naughty Piglets
description: Brixton natural-wine small-plates restaurant — an early-adopter of the format, still a neighbourhood favourite.
tips: Natural wine list is one of London's best.

name: Salon
description: A Brixton Village 20-seater — small plates, local sourcing, seasonal menus that change weekly.
tips: Book ahead. Tasting menu £60.

name: Boqueria
description: Iconic Brixton and Battersea Spanish tapas bars — authentic, loud, generous with the sherry list.
tips: Brixton bar opens late.

name: Fatto a Mano
description: Islington Neapolitan pizzeria — from the popular Brighton mother-ship, with proper 00 flour pizza.
tips: Family-friendly. Good gluten-free option.

name: Yard Sale Pizza
description: Local-favourite London pizza chain — thin-crust New York-style, neighbourhood delivery since 2014.
tips: Collaborations with other London food businesses on monthly specials.

name: Voodoo Rays
description: Dalston's late-night pizza slice shop — New York-style slices, vegan options, open until 4am on weekends.
tips: Great end-of-night pizza.

name: The Ladbroke Arms
description: A Notting Hill gastropub — cosy, good beer and cider list, genuinely great Sunday roasts.
tips: Popular with the Notting Hill crowd.

name: The Harwood Arms
description: Britain's only Michelin-starred pub — seasonal British cooking in a Fulham gastropub with a long-time devoted following.
tips: Game in season is essential. Book 3 weeks ahead.

name: The Camberwell Arms
description: The Anchor & Hope team's Camberwell gastropub — muscular British cooking and an unpretentious atmosphere.
tips: Feast menu for 4+ £40pp.

name: The Eagle
description: London's original gastropub (1991) — not a gastropub but *the* gastropub, Farringdon's bar that invented a genre.
tips: The Bife Ana steak sandwich is the original signature dish.

name: The Anchor & Hope
description: Waterloo gastropub — no-reservations (except for Sunday lunch), bold seasonal British food since 2003.
tips: Sunday lunch bookable one sitting 2pm — arrive for sherry first.

name: Quality Wines
description: Sister to Quality Chop House — a Farringdon wine bar-counter, big natural-wine list, bar-stool classic.
tips: £14 lunch at the bar is a steal.

name: Ducksoup
description: Dean Street natural-wine bar and small-plates restaurant — daily-changing handwritten menu, counter-first.
tips: Walk-in first. Hand-written menu and extraordinary vinyl collection.

name: Rita's
description: Dalston-Soho counter for coney-island corn dogs, American dive food, and a lively bar — a cult Soho favourite.
tips: Corn dog is the signature. Frosé in summer.

name: Frizzante at Hackney City Farm
description: Café inside Hackney City Farm — excellent Italian brunch, homemade pasta, family-friendly.
tips: The polenta with ragù is legendary for brunch.

name: Caravan Exmouth
description: Exmouth Market all-day restaurant — coffee roaster + globally-influenced menu; weekend brunch a reliable hit.
tips: Cornbread with maple butter is the classic.

name: Fortnum & Mason Diamond Jubilee Tea Salon
description: Afternoon tea on the 4th floor of Fortnum & Mason — the most London of afternoon teas.
tips: Book 8 weeks ahead. 18 varieties of tea.

name: Tea at Claridge's
description: The Foyer at Claridge's — England's most photographed afternoon tea, in Art Deco splendour.
tips: Book 3 months ahead. Strictly smart-casual.

name: Afternoon Tea at The Savoy
description: The Thames Foyer at The Savoy — dome-ceilinged, piano-soundtracked afternoon tea, a Regency-era ritual.
tips: Themed teas rotate; vegan menu available.

name: Brown's Hotel English Tea Room
description: Britain's oldest hotel afternoon tea (since 1837) — an intimate, wood-panelled Mayfair salon of proper old-school style.
tips: Includes a stand-alone 'English Afternoon Tea' menu.

name: Afternoon Tea at The Ritz
description: The most famous afternoon tea in the world — in the Palm Court of The Ritz, with a strict jacket-and-tie policy.
tips: Book 3-6 months ahead. Strict dress code.

name: Diwana Bhel Poori House
description: 1970s Drummond Street Indian — the chaat-and-dosa institution that predates most Asian-British food institutions.
tips: Lunch buffet £11 vegetarian. BYOB.

name: Masala Zone
description: Popular mid-range Indian chain, six branches — thali platters, street-food dishes, a good group-dining choice.
tips: Grand thali menu is excellent value.

name: Patara
description: Upscale Thai chain with Mayfair, Soho, and Knightsbridge branches — reliable refined Thai in elegant rooms.
tips: Lunch set £22.

name: Busaba Eathai
description: Alan Yau's Thai canteen — communal benches, quick service, strong pad Thai. Multiple central branches.
tips: Go early to avoid queues.

name: Wagamama Soho
description: The UK's original Wagamama — the Streatham Street original is gone, but the Soho branch is closest in spirit.
tips: Chicken katsu curry is the national dish. Bench seating family-friendly.

name: Three Uncles
description: Cantonese roast meats — char siu pork, roast duck, soy-poached chicken — counter-style in Brixton, Camden, and Liverpool Street.
tips: Roast duck noodles — the signature.

name: Panda Dim Sum
description: Islington dim sum specialist — hand-rolled dumplings, xiao long bao, and Cantonese favourites.
tips: BYOB — small corkage fee.

name: Hakkasan Hanway Place
description: The original Hakkasan, in Fitzrovia — Michelin-starred Cantonese in a moody-lit basement since 2001.
tips: Lunch dim sum menu cheaper than dinner.

name: Yauatcha Soho Basement
description: Yauatcha's basement cocktail lounge and dim sum all-day — same kitchen, louder vibe.
tips: Cocktail bar accepts walk-ins; dinner bookable.

name: Ciao Bella
description: A cult Lamb's Conduit Street trattoria — candlelit, pianist on the piano nightly, classic Italian menu since 1982.
tips: Big tables for groups. Piano from 8pm.

name: Andina Shoreditch
description: Peruvian-inspired small plates in Redchurch Street — mix of ceviche, tiraditos, and Peruvian cocktails.
tips: The ceviche mixto is essential.

name: Juniper & Rye
description: Soho gin-and-whisky-bar-restaurant — Scottish-inspired small plates, 150+ gins behind the counter.
tips: G&T flights pair with cheese boards.

name: Frog by Adam Handling
description: Covent Garden Michelin-starred British — Adam Handling's flagship, a bright dining room, seasonal tasting menus.
tips: Cheese tasting bar downstairs is a real treat.

name: Lino
description: A Fitzrovia modern European — pasta, seasonal small plates, airy atrium dining room.
tips: Lunch set £22 weekdays.

name: Old Queen Street Café
description: Westminster café by chef Kevin McManus — loved for civil-servant lunches and refined bar-forward dinners.
tips: Celebrity-ministerial crowd at lunch.

name: Speedboat Bar
description: Soho's new Thai-Chinese-leaning small-plates bar — wood-fired cooking, buzzy upstairs room.
tips: Walk-in-friendly downstairs.

name: Bacchanalia
description: Richard Caring's neoclassical Mayfair showpiece — a glamorous Mediterranean dining room flanked by ancient sculptures.
tips: Dining room is a curated gallery of Greek and Roman pieces.

name: Leong's Legend
description: Chinatown Taiwanese restaurant — Taipei-style xiao long bao, bubble tea, authentic Taiwanese dishes.
tips: Ice shavings with condensed milk for dessert.

name: Monmouth Café at Borough
description: Monmouth Coffee's sit-down café at Borough Market — pastries, perfectly made filter coffee, lively market atmosphere.
tips: Closed Sundays. Be prepared to queue.
